evidence: The accepted native_frame_segment_tick still reloads rt_ctx, native_call_row, dispatcher/audit flags and row metadata before its active/blocked/type checks. The packed scope already validates owned known rows; the active index already proves current Bool-true eligibility.
candidate: Extend the private owned-frame capability to bypass repeated row/context/type and active checks, rather than relying only on skipping the display-array read.
required_proof: Audit every rt_ctx/native_call_row/f_ctx write; invalidate field replacement and any dynamic boundary. Do not assume ordinary C++ fields are immutable.
Separate metadata/eligibility capability from default-display capability; preserve nondefault and foreign fallbacks.
Keep captured array order/length, current data, metadata diagnostics and all numeric operations unchanged.
The active-index recovery lambda must recheck eligibility/structure/epoch and pass no trusted capability after mutations.
Gem.character getter calls remain a callback boundary; recheck any capability whose proof can be invalidated there.
Actual-DLL directed counterexamples plus all formal fixed200/2604/raw24 gates remain mandatory.

concrete_design.scope_owner_rows: Record a private per-character array of {owner, exact initial NativeMethodRow, owned CoreContext, Gem type bit}, without enlarging GdObj/GdArr/BattleCtx or the active-index entry.
concrete_design.callback_interface: Use an optional item_index argument in active_cooldown_visit via is_invocable; existing one-argument callbacks remain unchanged. Indexed calls pass the captured original index. Recovery calls omit it and receive no metadata capability.
concrete_design.per_phase: Prepare one token bound to an enrolled character, structural version and epoch, plus its owner-row view. An unenrolled character must receive no default-display or metadata capability.
concrete_design.per_owner: Before the tick, select a row only when the original index and current owner pointer match. At tick entry recheck structure/epoch/watch/registry, current rt_ctx, current row pointer and current f_ctx pointer. A mismatch executes the complete existing header.
concrete_design.fast_body: Bypass only repeated row/context/audit/type-table checks; keep the physical active Bool and blocked-epoch checks. Cache the Gem type result, compensating the original diagnostic hit at its original position.
concrete_design.getter_boundary: Capture the context reference at the original point before Gem.character. Keep the default-display version recheck at the actual read after the getter; do not abort a tick merely because eligibility changed after its original entry check.
concrete_design.cpp_copy: GdObj assignment clears the current row, which the live pointer comparison catches. No unsupported const-row rewrites or placement-new assumptions should be introduced.
concrete_design.shared_proof_amortization: Reuse the validated metadata capability for the Null read on non-Gem items, because no user callback occurs before that read. Gems still recheck the version at the actual read after character(). This is a new source variant, not a rerun of the rejected view.

validation_additions: Unenrolled same-context third character with a nondefault override must use the old read path.
Clear/replace the cached row, change the current rt_ctx or f_ctx, toggle dispatcher/audit flags, and verify the full fallback.
Mutations in a Gem getter must observe the original pre-getter context and post-getter override read.
Preserve all old counters, not merely the new fast-path counter.
